Class BootstrapDispatcher

java.lang.Object
com.macstab.chaos.jvm.instrumentation.bridge.BootstrapDispatcher
public final class BootstrapDispatcher extends Object
Bootstrap-classloader-resident static dispatcher that routes intercepted JDK operations to the chaos runtime.

Classloader isolation

ByteBuddy @Advice classes woven into JDK methods (e.g. Thread.start(), System.currentTimeMillis()) execute in whatever classloader loaded the target class — which for JDK classes is the bootstrap classloader. Normal agent classes live in the agent classloader and are therefore invisible to bootstrap-loaded code.

To bridge this gap, BootstrapDispatcher is packaged into a temporary JAR and appended to the bootstrap classpath at agent startup (via Instrumentation.appendToBootstrapClassLoaderSearch). Once loaded by the bootstrap classloader, it is visible to all instrumented JDK code and can be called directly from advice.

MethodHandle bridge

The actual ChaosRuntime implementation lives in the agent classloader and is unreachable by name from bootstrap code. The bridge is established at startup via install(Object, MethodHandle[]): the agent classloader passes in a BridgeDelegate instance (as Object to avoid class-not-found errors in bootstrap code) and a pre-built MethodHandle[] of size HANDLE_COUNT. Each element is an unbound virtual MethodHandle resolved against the BridgeDelegate interface; every dispatch call supplies the delegate instance as the first argument at invocation time. Integer constants (DECORATE_EXECUTOR_RUNNABLE … BEFORE_JMX_GET_ATTR) serve as stable indices into this array.

Reentrancy guard

Chaos processing itself calls instrumented JDK methods (e.g. Thread.sleep, System.currentTimeMillis). Without protection this would recurse infinitely. The DEPTH ThreadLocal counts nested dispatch calls on the current thread. If DEPTH > 0 when a dispatch method is entered, the method returns its safe fallback immediately without invoking the delegate. The same per-thread array also holds the call-depth scope counters (see enterScope(int)), so it is kept for the thread's lifetime rather than removed on unwind.

Thread safety

Both delegate and handles are volatile. Each dispatch method snapshot-reads both fields into local variables before use; this eliminates time-of-check / time-of-use races across the two-field publication protocol used by install(Object, MethodHandle[]).

Lifecycle

install(Object, MethodHandle[]) must be called exactly once before any dispatch method can route to the delegate. Before install, all dispatch methods return their documented fallback values, allowing the JVM to start cleanly without chaos enabled.

    SCOPE_JDBC_INTERNAL
    Scope of a JDBC driver's or connection pool's own work (scope-only): Connection.isValid(int) of every driver, and HikariCP's validation, connection set-up and reset and its rollback of a connection taken back dirty (PoolBase.isConnectionDead, newPoolEntry, resetConnectionState, ProxyConnection.close).
    static final int
    SCOPE_JDBC_PREPARE
    Scope index for Connection.prepareStatement / prepareCall overloads.
    static final int
    SCOPE_JDBC_ROLLBACK
    Scope index for Connection.rollback (proxy → driver).
    static final int
    SCOPE_JDK_COMPLETION
    A one-shot consumable marker, not a call depth: set when a JDK timer starts ( CompletableFuture$Timeout.run, and $DelayedCompleter.run on JDK 21), consumed by the first completion the timer makes (consumeScope(int)), which is not evaluated, and cleared by the timer's exit advice on every path: a timer that completes nothing (its future is already done) leaves no marker for the next completion on its thread.
    static final int
    SCOPE_JDK_INTERNAL
    Scope of the JDK's own use of a general primitive (L3a, scope-only): ClassLoader.loadClass, sun.nio.ch.Util.getTemporaryDirectBuffer / getTemporaryAlignedDirectBuffer, java.nio.Bits.reserveMemory, FileChannelImpl.mapInternal and, on JDK 21, a CompletableFuture$Delayer.delay of a JDK timer.
    static final int
    SCOPE_JMX
    Scope index for MBeanServer.invoke / getAttribute (server → interceptor).
    static final int
    SCOPE_MESSAGE_SEND
    Scope of a Kafka KafkaProducer.send(record, callback) (scope-only): the producer's metadata wait inside it is the send's evaluation point, the same wait from partitionsFor is not a send.
    static final int
    SCOPE_POOL_WORKER
    Scope index held while a thread pool creates a worker (ThreadPoolExecutor.addWorker): a thread started there serves many tasks and must not inherit the starter's session.
    static final int
    SCOPE_QUEUE
    Scope index for BlockingQueue put / offer / take / poll (bridges, put → offer).
    static final int
    SCOPE_REDIS_SETUP
    Scope of a Jedis connection's own set-up and of a pool's validation ( Connection.initializeFromClientConfig, Connection.ping, validateObject / activateObject of the connection factories): the commands sent inside it are the client's, not the application's, and are not REDIS_COMMANDs.
    static final int
    SCOPE_RESOURCE_LOAD
    Scope index for ClassLoader.getResource (parent delegation).
    static final int
    SCOPE_SERIALIZATION
    Scope of ObjectOutputStream.writeObject / ObjectInputStream.readObject: one serialization of the object graph, not one per nested object a class's own writeObject / readObject writes or reads.
    static final int

  • Method Details

    • enterScope

      public static boolean enterScope(int scope)
      Enters a call-depth scope on the current thread.

      Advice must pair every call with exactly one exitScope(int): from the OnMethodExit(onThrowable = Throwable.class) advice on normal and exceptional exits, and from the enter advice itself when the dispatch it performed throws (ByteBuddy does not run exit advice when enter advice throws).

      Parameters:
      scope - one of the SCOPE_* constants
      Returns:
      true when this is the outermost call of the scope on the current thread, i.e. the call that should be evaluated

    • inScope

      public static boolean inScope(int scope)
      Whether the current thread is inside a call-depth scope, without entering it: for advice that only asks where it runs.
      Parameters:
      scope - one of the SCOPE_* constants
      Returns:
      true when a call of the scope is on the current thread's stack

    • consumeScope

      public static boolean consumeScope(int scope)
      Consumes a one-shot marker (SCOPE_JDK_COMPLETION): clears it and reports whether it was set. Also the way the marker's owner clears it on exit.
      Parameters:
      scope - one of the SCOPE_* constants used as a marker
      Returns:
      true when the marker was set on the current thread

    • exitScope

      public static boolean exitScope(int scope)
      Leaves a call-depth scope entered with enterScope(int).
      Parameters:
      scope - one of the SCOPE_* constants
      Returns:
      true when the outermost call of the scope has now left it

    • beginInternalCall

      public static void beginInternalCall()
      Marks the start of agent-internal work on the current thread that runs outside a dispatch, such as the reflective URL and pool-name extraction in the HTTP and JDBC advice. While marked, every dispatch returns its fallback, so the agent's own Method.invoke calls are not evaluated as application reflection. Must be paired with endInternalCall() in a finally block.

    • endInternalCall

      public static void endInternalCall()
      Ends agent-internal work started with beginInternalCall().

    • isDepthThreadLocal

      public static boolean isDepthThreadLocal(Object threadLocal)
      Whether threadLocal is the dispatcher's own depth counter: the ThreadLocal advice skips it so that reading the depth does not re-enter the advice. Identity, not equals.
      Parameters:
      threadLocal - the ThreadLocal being read or written
      Returns:
      true for the depth counter

    • install

      public static void install(@Nullable Object bridgeDelegate, MethodHandle @Nullable [] methodHandles)
      Wires the delegate and its pre-built method handles into this dispatcher.

      Must be called exactly once, by the agent classloader, after this class has been loaded into the bootstrap classloader. The write order — handles before delegate — is intentional: a racing reader that snapshots a non-null delegate is guaranteed to also see a non-null handles array.

      Parameters:
      bridgeDelegate - the BridgeDelegate instance from the agent classloader; passed as Object to avoid a ClassNotFoundException in bootstrap code
      methodHandles - array of exactly HANDLE_COUNT MethodHandle instances, indexed by the public integer constants defined on this class; each handle is an unbound virtual handle resolved against BridgeDelegate, and dispatch calls pass bridgeDelegate as the first argument on every invocation

    • installedDelegate

      public static @Nullable Object installedDelegate()
      Returns the delegate wired by install(Object, MethodHandle[]), or null when none is installed. Used by the installer to detect a second copy of the agent, loaded by another class loader, before it replaces the first copy's delegate: the dispatcher is JVM-wide (bootstrap-loaded) while each agent copy has its own runtime.
      Returns:
      the installed delegate, or null

    • claimRevision

      public static @Nullable String claimRevision(@Nullable String revision)
      Claims this bridge for one agent revision (a digest of the bridge class bytes the agent copy appended), so a copy of another version detects that its own bridge classes are not the ones the bootstrap class loader resolves. Set-once: the first claim wins and a later claim never overwrites it, it returns the claimed revision instead; this also settles two copies in different class loaders that both appended a bridge before either resolved one.
      Parameters:
      revision - the claiming copy's revision, or null to read the claimed revision without claiming
      Returns:
      the revision claimed before this call, or null when there was none (then revision, unless null, is claimed now)

    • decorateExecutorRunnable

      public static Runnable decorateExecutorRunnable(String operation, @Nullable Object executor, Runnable task) throws Throwable
      Gives the active chaos scenario an opportunity to wrap the submitted runnable before it is handed to the executor.
      Parameters:
      operation - a string tag identifying the submission call site (e.g. "execute", "submit"); never null
      executor - the Executor that will run the task; may be null when the calling context is not an executor subclass
      task - the runnable to potentially wrap; never null
      Returns:
      the (possibly wrapped) runnable; equals task when the dispatcher is not yet installed, when the reentrancy guard fires, or when no active scenario applies
      Throws:
      Throwable - if the delegate throws — propagated to the advice via sneaky-throw

    • decorateExecutorCallable

      public static <T> Callable<T> decorateExecutorCallable(String operation, @Nullable Object executor, Callable<T> task) throws Throwable
      Gives the active chaos scenario an opportunity to wrap the submitted callable before it is handed to the executor.
      Type Parameters:
      T - the callable's return type
      Parameters:
      operation - a string tag identifying the submission call site; never null
      executor - the executor that will run the task; may be null
      task - the callable to potentially wrap; never null
      Returns:
      the (possibly wrapped) callable; equals task as the fallback
      Throws:
      Throwable - if the delegate throws

      Throws:
      Throwable - if an active scenario injects an exception to suppress the start

    • afterNioSelect

      public static void afterNioSelect(Object selector, boolean spurious)
      Called after a selector's select, also one the agent skipped. A select that ran for real has returned, so the JDK consumed any wakeup made before or while it ran: a wakeup kept for the selector meanwhile (SELECT_WAKEUPS) is dropped, whenever it was recorded (also before the select was entered, or before a scenario was activated). A wakeup made after the native select returned but before this runs is dropped too: the next stall then runs its full length, the conservative side.
      Parameters:
      selector - the selector
      spurious - whether the agent skipped the real select (the enter advice's flag)

      Throwable - if an active scenario injects a failure

    • corruptionSeed

      public static long corruptionSeed()
      Returns the seed of the bit flip the scenario chose for the current thread's read, so a fixed randomSeed corrupts the same bit; random when the agent is not installed.
      Returns:
      the seed

    • isArchive

      public static boolean isArchive(@Nullable String path)
      Whether path is an archive the JVM reads classes from (.jar, .zip, .jmod). ZipFile reads such archives through a shared RandomAccessFile: it seeks, then reads. A dispatch between the two can load classes from the same archive, which moves the file pointer and makes the outer read return the wrong bytes. Archive reads are class loading, so they are not evaluated at all.
      Parameters:
      path - the file path, or null
      Returns:
      true for an archive

    • corruptBuffer

      public static void corruptBuffer(ByteBuffer buffer, int count)
      Flips one random bit in the count bytes a channel read just put into buffer (the bytes before its position).
      Parameters:
      buffer - the buffer the read filled
      count - the number of bytes the read returned; nothing happens when <= 0

    • corruptByte

      public static int corruptByte(int value)
      Flips one random bit of a byte returned by a single-byte read().
      Parameters:
      value - the value the read returned
      Returns:
      the corrupted value, or value at end of stream (-1)
